correctness.rationale: The complete three-idempotent formula for the fixed Cesaro average follows by integrating distinct frequencies. Direct SRG algebra yields exact diagonal/edge/nonedge Schur squares; the nonprincipal eigenvalue rational identity was verified symbolically with no floating assumptions. In all integral cases r>=1,s<=-2; all irrational cases have equal Galois-conjugate multiplicities and are conference graphs, hence either C5 or r>=1,s<=-2. The stated first nonprincipal eigenvalue is positive because its first term is nonnegative and second strictly positive. The complement shares all three spectral projectors and gives positivity of the second restricted mode. C5 has exact eigenvalues 1 and 1/5. The constant mode is 1 by stochasticity. Five exact graph computations and two global rational-function identities were replayed at the packaged verify.py; no finite run substitutes for unrestricted case division.

originality.rationale: arXiv:2404.02236 (initial preprint §4, Open Problem 4.1) explicitly asks for full ordinary average-mixing rank on all primitive distance-regular graphs. This result proves the entire diameter-two strongly regular subcase by sign inequalities for both nonprincipal modes, complement symmetry, and a separate conference-graph case. Earlier spectral/Gram formulas do not by themselves supply the universal strict positivity. A 2026 paper on selected sampling laws shares formulas but not this universal Cesaro rank theorem. The database and literature comparisons identified no equal or stronger theorem; unindexed association-scheme coverage remains possible.
residual_risks: An equivalent positive-definiteness consequence could be proved under association-scheme Krein parameters or a differently indexed classical formulation; none was found in checked sources.
Primitive higher-diameter distance-regular graph rank remains unresolved by this argument.
The 2026 moment-method paper has overlapping projector formulas, although its chosen-law uniform mixing conclusions have different quantifiers.

value.rationale: The class of primitive strongly regular graphs is the entire diameter-two case of the full-rank question explicitly posed as Open Problem 4.1 in the 2024 open preprint. Strict positivity excludes any lost long-time transition-probability mode and is stronger than semidefiniteness or tabulating ranks for examples. The structural complement argument and the exceptional conference case resolve a natural infinite family without claiming the full higher-diameter question. It is a motivated problem, not an arbitrary narrow graph order or a known table recomputation.
